sections.h2: Where is the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds and how do I reach it?
sections.html:
The Charlevoix County Register of Deeds sits at 13513 Division Street in the city of Charlevoix, MI 49720. The state treasury list of registers of deeds gives the phone as 231-547-7204 and the fax as 231-237-0106, and the office takes email at rod@charlevoixcounty.org. Call before you drive in, because the office page does not post public counter hours.

Charlevoix is the county seat, and Boyne City is the largest city. Anyone selling a house in the county, whether it is a Lake Charlevoix cottage, a place in East Jordan, or a home on Beaver Island, finishes the transfer at this one office. The county Register of Deeds page describes the office as a constitutional office created in 1835 that records, indexes and preserves land documents.

sections.h2: What does the Register of Deeds do when I sell a house in Charlevoix County?
sections.html:
It receives your deed, time stamps it, assigns a liber and page number, scans it and adds it to the searchable index. That is the step that puts a new owner on the public record for the property.

The office is blunt about its limits. Its own page says recording a document does not make the document legal, it makes the document public. Staff do not hand out blank deed forms and cannot draft or advise on one, since MCL 600.916(1) bars clerks from giving legal advice. A title company or an attorney prepares the deed, and the register of deeds checks that it meets the recording rules.

  • Deeds, mortgages, land contracts and discharges are recorded here.
  • The computer image index reaches back to January 1984, and older records are still being indexed.
  • Documents can be hand delivered or mailed in with the fee and a self-addressed stamped envelope.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Charlevoix County?
sections.html:
The base charge is $30.00 per document, no matter how many pages it has. That amount follows MCL 600.2567, and the county fee page notes that $4.00 of it goes to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation Fund.

Charlevoix County Register of Deeds statutory fees (county fee page)
ItemCharge
Recording one document$30.00
Each extra liber and page on an assignment or discharge covering several instruments$3.00
Tax certification$5.00
Copies of documents$1.00 per page
Plat copies$4.00 per page
Certified copy$5.00

One check payable to the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds can cover the recording fee, any transfer tax and the tax certification together. Since January 2, 2025, the office adds $3.00 per document for return postage when you send a document in without a prepaid return envelope, and it holds the document unrecorded until that amount arrives.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Charlevoix County home sale?
sections.html:
Two taxes apply to most sales. The county tax is 55 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 under MCL 207.504, which sets that rate for counties under 2,000,000 people. The state tax is $3.75 for each $500 or fraction under MCL 207.525.

Put together, a sale at $276,800, the Census median value of owner-occupied homes in the county, runs 554 units of $500. That means about $305 in county tax and about $2,078 in state tax. The deed must show the total value on its face, or an affidavit with the value must be attached.

Some transfers fall outside the county tax. MCL 207.505 lists instruments with consideration under $100, security instruments such as mortgages, leases, and deeds that only correct a title flaw. Ask the register of deeds how your particular deed is treated before closing day.

sections.h2: What must a deed look like to be accepted in Charlevoix County?
sections.html:
It must meet the page rules in MCL 565.201, and the register of deeds cannot accept a deed that misses them. Most rejections come from formatting, so check the sheet before you mail it.

  • Margin: at least 2.5 inches of blank space at the top of the first page and half an inch on the other sides of every page.
  • Print: 10-point type or larger, black ink, on white paper of 20-pound weight or heavier.
  • Size: sheets no smaller than 8.5 by 11 inches and no larger than 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • First line: a single statement naming the recordable event, such as a warranty deed.
  • Only one recordable event per instrument.

The statute also wants a legible printed name under each signature that matches the acknowledgment, plus the drafter's name and business address on any instrument signed after 1964.

sections.h2: Why do I need a tax certificate before a warranty deed is recorded in Charlevoix County?
sections.html:
Michigan law makes the register of deeds ask for proof that no tax liens stand against the parcel. MCL 211.135 calls for county treasurer certification that taxes for the five years before the deed date are paid, and the Charlevoix office charges $5.00 for the certification.

The county fee page names the deeds that trigger this step: warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts, and trustee, fiduciary or personal representative deeds with a warranty clause. It also covers master deeds for condominiums. A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenants is excluded by MCL 211.135(6)(e), so it moves through without the certificate. Start at the County Treasurer's Office first, then bring the certificate with the deed.

sections.h2: How can I search records or guard my title in Charlevoix County?
sections.html:
The county offers three search routes and a free fraud alert. Webtecs is the free portal for taxpayers and occasional users, and images can be bought document by document. Laredo Anywhere is a subscription service for people who run title searches regularly, and the office asks for an email to rod@charlevoixcounty.org to request an agreement. Tapestry is a web search that needs no subscription.

Homeowners can also sign up for Property Fraud Alert, which emails the owner when a document is recorded under their name. That helps after a sale too, since a seller can watch for a deed or lien appearing against a property they believed they had cleared.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about selling a house in Charlevoix County?
sections.html:
Charlevoix County is a high-value market for northern Michigan. The Census Bureau lists the 2025 population at 26,036 and shows 18,026 housing units. Owners occupy 83.5% of homes, median gross rent is $949, and the median household income for 2020 to 2024 is $76,531.

The 2020 count showed 35.4% of housing units vacant, which points to a large stock of seasonal and second homes. Builders pulled 111 permits in 2025. Water covers 70% of the county's 1,390 square miles, and the 416 square miles of land make it the fourth smallest county in Michigan by land area, so waterfront parcels and island properties often carry details that the deed and title search have to capture accurately.

faqs.q: How much does the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: It charges $30.00 per document regardless of page count. A tax certification adds $5.00 when the deed type requires one, and a document mailed without a prepaid return envelope adds $3.00 for postage. Transfer tax is separate and is figured on the sale price.

faqs.q: Can the Charlevoix County office prepare my deed for me?
faqs.a: No. Staff cannot draft documents or give legal advice because MCL 600.916(1) bars clerks from doing so, and the office does not supply blank deed forms. An attorney or title company should prepare the deed before you bring it in for recording.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax certificate for a quitclaim deed in Charlevoix County?
faqs.a: Usually not. MCL 211.135(6)(e) exempts a quitclaim deed or other conveyance with no covenants of warranty from the certificate rule. Warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts and certain fiduciary deeds do need the County Treasurer's certification first.

faqs.q: How do I pay the transfer tax on a Charlevoix County sale?
faqs.a: Pay it with the recording. The county fee page says checks for transfer tax and tax certification should be made payable to the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds and may be combined with the recording fee in one check. The county rate is 55 cents and the state rate is $3.75 per $500.

faqs.q: How can I get a copy of a recorded Charlevoix County deed?
faqs.a: Search the free Webtecs portal and buy the image, or ask the office. The county fee page lists copies at $1.00 per page and certified copies at $5.00, so ask the office for the exact total on a long document.
